_comment: Template-fleet membership exclusions. Default rule: every directory under Projects/ whose name starts with 'co-' is a fleet member, minus the ids listed in excluded[]. L0-only — never propagated to templates/ or scaffolded projects, never added to any propagation map. Consumers: scripts/lib/fleet.ts (sole code path) and scripts/fleet-list.ts. Design: docs/designs/2026-11-07-fleet-membership-ssot-design.md

excluded.reason: Claude Code plugin distribution project (plugin.json + commands/), not a template-derived variant project: no variant.json, no template sync obligation; last template sync (2026-10-03, template 0.10.0) is historical residue, not an open obligation. Architecture map depicts the L3 fleet as 16 projects without it.

Git-worktree husk of the ROOT workspace repo (shared ../../.git, remote ai-workspace-standards), not a variant project: the Projects/co-* glob admits it whenever the directory exists, and its 'dirty status' was root leakage via upward git walk. Upgrades run against root-mirror content produce meaningless deliveries (T-20261119-007). Removed empty 2026-11-19 and recreated empty 2026-11-20 00:05 KST by tooling — the exclusion is defensive so a recreated husk can never rejoin the fleet. Mechanical derivation (DEC-20261107-01) stays authoritative; this row only pins the known non-members.

Git-worktree husk of the ROOT workspace repo (same shape as co-deck-worktrees): root-mirror content, no variant.json, no template sync obligation. Directory currently absent (removed 2026-11-19, verified empty rmdir-only); excluded defensively so a recreation can never rejoin the fleet (T-20261119-007).

Adoption-only variant and a worktree-mirror of the out-of-tree QuickDL adoption site (design 2026-11-21-co-utility-dedup-and-adoption-role-design §5.7): the upgrade engine refuses it by its variant.json consumption flag, and the daily resync audit already skips it with an informational line. The row keeps every loop consumer (resync audit, backport batteries, fleet reports) from meeting it through the Projects/co-* glob.
